## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pakkagodhajātaka* (Ja 333), translated as "The Cooked Lizard", is a canonical story preserved in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to the narrative framework recorded in the commentary, the Buddha told this story while staying at Jetavana regarding a certain landowner. In the core verse edited by V. Fausböll, a queen addresses the royal king (*rathesabha*), stating that his true character was recognized in the midst of the forest when a roasted monitor lizard escaped on the branch of an *assattha* tree (*assatthadumasākhāya pakkagodhā palāyathā 'ti*) [Fausböll 1883]. The commentary explains the verse in detail, glossing *tirīṭino* and clarifying that *pakkā* means roasted over embers (*aṅgārapakkā*) [Fausböll 1883].
